recentItems.title: MARIUPOL, BAKHMUT, AVDIIVKA — BEFORE AND AFTER: how the war changed Ukrainian cities
recentItems.description:
Bakhmut, Mariinka, Vuhledar, Popasna, Sievierodonetsk, Avdiivka and Mariupol — this special report shows how Ukrainian cities changed after large-scale hostilities and the establishment of Russian control. Where residential neighbourhoods, businesses, schools, hospitals and developed urban infrastructure once stood, large areas now lie in ruins.

Russia promised residents of the captured territories “peace,” “development” and a “new life.” Russian state media showcase renovated façades, new facilities, flags and public events. At the same time, this report focuses on the scale of the destruction and the problems faced by local residents: damaged homes and infrastructure, and difficulties with water supply, heating and communications.

What remains of the cities over which some of the fiercest battles of the war were fought? What do Mariupol, Bakhmut, Avdiivka, Popasna, Mariinka, Vuhledar and Sievierodonetsk look like today? And what is left out of reports about the “reconstruction” of the occupied territories? Watch the new episode of Special Report.

recentItems.title: STRIKE BEHIND RUSSIAN LINES: Ammunition depots and an attack UAV launch site hit
recentItems.description:
Overnight, Ukraine’s Defence Forces struck a number of Russian military facilities in temporarily occupied territories. The targets included sites associated with the use of unmanned systems, as well as ammunition depots.

In temporarily occupied Donetsk, a facility used by Russian forces to store, prepare and launch attack UAVs was hit. Several other targets were attacked in the occupied part of Luhansk region, where two Russian army ammunition depots were reportedly struck.

Meanwhile, intense fighting continues along the front line. Over the past 24 hours, 221 combat engagements were recorded. The Pokrovsk sector remains one of the most heavily contested areas, with Ukraine’s Defence Forces repelling 26 Russian attacks.

Russian army losses also remain high. According to the Ukrainian side, Russia lost 1,690 personnel over the past day. Fighting continues simultaneously in various sectors of the front, while Ukrainian forces strike Russian military facilities behind the lines in the occupied territories.

recentItems.title: Moscow LOST a key refinery: Ukraine deployed ROBOTS behind Russian lines and cut off a FUEL route
recentItems.description:
The Moscow Oil Refinery suspended oil processing after an attack on September 20. The Gazprom Neft facility, which processed approximately 11.6 million tonnes of crude oil in 2024, sustained damage to its primary refining units. According to Reuters sources, repairs could take several weeks. In the following days, strikes also hit oil-refining facilities in Ufa and Russia’s Samara region.

On the front line, the Third Army Corps continues Operation Vivaldi. According to the corps, during its two stages, Ukrainian forces brought 125 square kilometres of territory back under Ukrainian control, including 50 square kilometres of de-occupied land. During the operation, Ukrainian forces also employed an unusual tactic: heavy drones delivered unmanned ground systems more than 10 kilometres behind Russian lines.

Another area of focus is strikes against Russian logistics. The report covers the destruction of a fuel pipeline that, according to the Third Corps, supplied approximately half of the daily diesel needs of Russia’s West Grouping of Forces, as well as strikes on drone bases, bridges and other supply infrastructure.

recentItems.title: Ilsky Oil Refinery ablaze — Kyiv under drone attack: residential building and kindergarten hit
recentItems.description:
Ukraine’s defense forces reported a strike on the Ilsky oil refinery in Russia’s Krasnodar Krai. A fire broke out at the facility. The refinery’s capacity is around 7 million tons of oil per year, and its products, according to the Ukrainian General Staff, are used in part to supply Russian troops.

Meanwhile, Russia carried out another large-scale attack on Ukraine. In Kyiv, a Russian drone hit a residential building: a fire started, dozens of apartments were damaged, and there were casualties. In the city’s Obolon district, a Shahed drone reportedly struck a kindergarten. In Zaporizhzhia, people were killed in a Russian strike, and among the injured was a child. Consequences of Russian strikes on September 26 were also reported in Odesa and other regions.

Special attention is given to developments in the US. Fourteen senators from both the Republican and Democratic parties have called on Donald Trump to withdraw Vladimir Putin’s invitation to the G20 summit in Miami. In their letter, they expressed concern that the Russian president’s participation could help normalize relations with Moscow amid the war against Ukraine.

recentItems.title: Russian Oil Refinery and Almaz-Antey plant hit: meanwhile, Ukraine receives a decision on Patriot
recentItems.description:
Several Russian regions came under drone attack during the night of September 25. In Perm, a fire was reported near one of Russia’s largest oil refineries. In Ulyanovsk, the target was the Iskra plant, which is linked to the Almaz-Antey concern. In Voronezh, a fire broke out at a major synthetic-rubber manufacturing facility.

Against this backdrop, Russia continues its attacks on Ukraine, with Kyiv coming under another strike. At the same time, important news emerged concerning Ukraine’s air defense: Volodymyr Zelenskyy said that Donald Trump had made a final decision to grant Ukraine licenses to produce missiles for Patriot systems. The exact timeline and scale of the future production have not yet been publicly announced.

The episode also covers negotiations on a possible energy and maritime ceasefire, the Kremlin’s position, U.S. sanctions pressure, preparations for a special tribunal, and the prospect of trilateral contacts between Ukraine, the United States, and Russia.
